newsitem.title: USA: Apache ratchets up Qarun oil production.
newsitem.headline: Apache ratchets up Qarun oil production.

text.p: Apache Corp Chairman Raymond Plank said production from the company's Qarun concession in Egypt was ratcheted up to 40,000 barrels per day on Thursday.
Apache, which tripled its contractor interest in the concession to 75 percent with its Phoenix Resource Companies merger last year, said the field had been producing at 29,000 barrels per day.
"That's way ahead of what the analysts have been looking for," Plank said of the boost in Qarun production.

The company also has been working with officials in Egypt to boost production from its Khalda concession, which was producing at an average 32,000 barrels per day, or 4,800 barrels per day net to Apache last year, he said.
"We are going to chew it up and kill it," he said of the company's concessions in Egpyt, where Apache is the country's largest leaseholder with interests on 28 million gross acres.

In the United States, where Apache has been frustrated by volatile natural gas prices, the company is seeking joint ventures with major oil companies in its core Midcontinent and Gulf Coast operating areas, Plank told Reuters.
Apache, which is seeking to nearly double its share price to $60 a share over the next three years, also formally approved plans to expand its operations in Poland, Plank said.
The company recently formed a joint venture there with partner FX Energy and has committed $5 million on seismic surveys and drilling, a company spokesman said.
"Apache expects to make its shareholders a potfull (of money), or we wouldn't be going there," he said.
